question: What is the primary purpose of introducing barium sulfate during a lower GI series?

options.A: It stimulates immediate peristalsis to empty the bowel.
options.B: It cleanses the mucosal lining of accumulated fecal matter.
options.C: It numbs the rectal sphincter to reduce cramping pain.
options.D: It acts as a radiopaque contrast medium to highlight the colon.

explanation: Barium sulfate absorbs X-rays effectively, creating a clear visual contrast of the internal walls of the large intestine on radiographic images. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h1)

question: When might a clinician choose a barium enema instead of a routine colonoscopy?

options.A: When visualization of mucosal polyps under 2mm is required
options.B: When direct tissue biopsy of a lesion is urgently needed
options.C: When the patient has an active bowel perforation risk
options.D: When evaluating long segments or incomplete colonoscopies

explanation: Barium studies are useful for viewing the entire length of the large bowel, particularly when an endoscope cannot pass through an obstruction. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h1)

question: The main finding associated with diverticular disease on a barium enema is...

options.A: diffuse shortening of the colon length
options.B: abnormal widening of the ileocecal valve
options.D: complete absence of the rectal vault

explanation: Diverticular disease causes small pouches, or diverticula, to form along the wall of the colon, which fill with barium during the procedure. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h2)

question: Which condition is an absolute contraindication for performing a barium enema due to high mortality risk?
explanation: Leaking barium into the sterile peritoneal cavity causes severe chemical peritonitis and is a dangerous medical emergency. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h3)

question: Why is a recent deep mucosal biopsy considered a risk factor for a barium enema?

options.A: The fresh tissue site may rupture under infusion pressure.
options.B: The biopsy site will completely neutralize the barium contrast.
options.C: Barium will instantly stain the biopsy site permanently black.
options.D: Enema fluid causes immediate local infection at the site.

explanation: Pressure from liquid and air can break open a recently compromised or surgically altered bowel wall, leading to leakage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h3)

question: Before scheduling a barium enema for a female patient of childbearing age, what must the nurse check?
explanation: Ionizing radiation used during fluoroscopy poses significant risks to a developing fetus, making pregnancy verification mandatory. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h4)

question: Why must the nurse inform the patient about the strong urge to defecate during the test?

options.A: To help the patient mentally prepare and hold the contrast in
options.B: To ensure the patient drinks extra water before the enema
options.C: To instruct the patient to immediately use the room restroom
options.D: To prompt the patient to request immediate pain relief drugs

explanation: Knowing that cramping and the urge to void are normal sensations helps patients cooperate and maintain the contrast enema without premature expulsion. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h4)

question: Why is a strict bowel cleansing protocol required before a barium enema?

options.A: Laxatives prevent severe cramping during the actual procedure.
options.B: Barium will not enter the rectum if stool is present inside.
options.C: Clear bowels speed up the elimination of the barium afterward.
options.D: Fecal residue can mimic polyps and obscure diagnostic findings.

explanation: Stool left in the colon creates shadows on the X-ray that radiologists can easily mistake for tumors or polyps. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h5)

question: A frail elderly patient is prescribed a rigorous bowel preparation. What is a primary nursing concern?

options.A: Sudden weight gain from fluid retention
options.B: Permanent loss of bowel control reflexes
options.D: Immediate development of a bowel blockage

explanation: Aggressive purgatives and clear liquid diets can quickly compromise vulnerable patients, leading to dangerous fluid and electrolyte shifts. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h5)

question: A patient becomes pale and dizzy with sweating during the barium infusion. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Immediate absorption of toxic barium into the bloodstream
options.B: Acute kidney failure triggered by the contrast fluid
options.C: An allergic reaction to the latex gloves used by staff
options.D: A vasovagal reaction from colonic distension and cramping

explanation: Stretching of the bowel wall can stimulate the vagus nerve, causing sudden drops in blood pressure and heart rate accompanied by diaphoresis and dizziness. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h6)

question: Why are frequent positional changes required during an air-contrast barium enema?

options.A: To evenly coat the colonic mucosal walls with the contrast medium
options.B: To help the patient expel the barium faster during the test
options.C: To prevent the rectal tip from falling out of position
options.D: To reduce the physical pressure on the lower lumbar spine

explanation: Moving the patient into different tilts ensures that both liquid barium and air spread uniformly across every section of the intestinal lining for better visualization. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h6)

question: What is a normal expected finding that the nurse should explain to the patient after a barium enema?

options.A: Rectal bleeding will occur for at least twenty-four hours.
options.B: Urine will turn dark brown due to systemic barium excretion.
options.C: Skin color will temporarily turn yellow from contrast absorption.
options.D: Stools will appear chalky white or light gray for a few days.

explanation: As the body clears the ingested or infused barium sulfate, bowel movements naturally take on a pale, chalky appearance. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h7)

question: What primary complication do post-procedure laxatives and high fluid intake help prevent?

options.A: Bacterial infection of the large intestine
options.D: Permanent paralysis of the rectal sphincter

explanation: Barium solidifies as water is absorbed in the colon; fluids and laxatives keep the mixture moving to prevent a dangerous blockage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h7)
